reason: The cited evidence confirms that refractory HEAs have poor ductility (E1, E2) and that TRIP can improve strength–ductility in a carbon-containing medium-entropy alloy (E3). However, no cited passage provides evidence that interstitial carbon dissolves in refractory HEAs, induces TRIP in them, or that TRIP mechanisms operate in refractory HEAs at all; these key premises are unsupported extrapolations from a different alloy system.
premises: Refractory HEAs suffer from poor room-temperature ductility/brittleness
Interstitial carbon can be dissolved in refractory HEAs without forming excessive brittle carbides
Interstitial carbon induces local lattice strain that triggers martensitic transformation (TRIP) in refractory HEAs
TRIP mechanisms simultaneously enhance strength and ductility in metallic alloys
Carbon addition and TRIP effects observed in non-refractory HEAs (e.g., Fe-Co-Cr-Ni-Mo-C) are transferable to refractory HEAs
